A.explanation: Halving $10\text{ N}$ to $5\text{ N}$ ignores vector addition and the $120^{\circ}$ angle between the forces at P.

B.explanation: With two equal $10\text{ N}$ vectors at $120^{\circ}$, the components perpendicular to the bisector cancel and the parallel components sum to $10\text{ N}$.

C.explanation: About $17\text{ N}$ is $10\cos 30^{\circ} + 10\cos 30^{\circ}$, which would apply for a $60^{\circ}$ angle between the forces, not $120^{\circ}$.

D.explanation: $20\text{ N}$ is the scalar sum $10 + 10$, which only applies if the two $10\text{ N}$ forces acted in the same direction.

hints: Notice the diagram at P shows two arrows both labelled $10\text{ N}$ with $120^{\circ}$ between them, so the forces are equal but not opposite or parallel.
Resolve one $10\text{ N}$ force into components parallel and perpendicular to the other $10\text{ N}$ force using $\cos 60^{\circ}$ and $\sin 60^{\circ}$ for the $60^{\circ}$ to the extension.
Add the components head-to-tail: the perpendicular parts partly cancel and the resultant magnitude follows from $F^2 = F_x^2 + F_y^2$ in $\text{N}$.
walkthrough: Place the two $10\text{ N}$ vectors tail-to-tail at P with $120^{\circ}$ between them, so the angle between one force and the extension of the other is $180^{\circ} - 120^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}$.
Take x along the horizontal $10\text{ N}$ force. Then $F_x = 10 + 10\cos 120^{\circ}$ and $F_y = 10\sin 120^{\circ}$.
Substitute with units: $F_x = 10\text{ N} + 10(-0.5)\text{ N} = 5.0\text{ N}$ and $F_y = 10(0.866)\text{ N} = 8.66\text{ N}$.
Find the magnitude: $F = \sqrt{F_x^2 + F_y^2} = \sqrt{5.0^2 + 8.66^2}\text{ N} = \sqrt{25 + 75}\text{ N} = \sqrt{100}\text{ N} = 10\text{ N}$.
